report.summary: Chunk 4 of 7: Contains _norm_class, _normalize_turn, _refusal_receipt functions and their docstrings/claims. No new symbols beyond these.

handoff.purpose: Defines _norm_class, _normalize_turn, _refusal_receipt with validation and envelope filling logic.

symbols.name: _norm_class
symbols.note: Validates independence_class dict must have exactly 'vendor' and 'family' keys.

symbols.name: _normalize_turn
symbols.note: Fills the dcouncil/1 turn envelope with validation and defaults.

symbols.name: _refusal_receipt
symbols.note: Creates a refused turn stand-in, optionally redacting identity.

claims.text: Independence is a property of WEIGHTS, not of endpoints: local ``qwen2.5-coder:7b`` and bench ``qwen2.5-coder:7b`` are one voice on two sockets. The class is (vendor, model family) and is mandatory.
claims.why: The claim about independence being a property of weights is not checkable against the code; only the validation logic for the dict is present.

claims.text: if not isinstance(ic, dict) or set(ic) != {"vendor", "family"}: raise ValueError
claims.why: The code checks exactly that condition.

claims.text: Fill the dcouncil/1 turn envelope, fail-closed. Absence is REPORTED, never guessed favourably.
claims.why: The claim about fail-closed and reporting absence is a design statement not fully verifiable from this code alone; the function does raise errors for missing required fields.

claims.text: actor must be council.<vendor>.<model> (ADR-010 actor-namespace rule; a bare name in a durable record is a defect, and a vendor without a model id is not reproducible)
claims.why: The regex _ACTOR_RE is not defined in this chunk; the claim about ADR-010 and reproducibility is uncheckable.

claims.text: status='refused' is MINTED by the secret floor, never asserted by a caller: a caller-authored refusal is an unverified claim that a scan happened
claims.why: The code raises ValueError if status == 'refused', enforcing that callers cannot set it.

claims.text: turn content {len(content)} chars exceeds MAX_CONTENT_CHARS {MAX_CONTENT_CHARS}: bound it before chaining, never after
claims.why: The code checks len(content) > MAX_CONTENT_CHARS and raises ValueError.

claims.text: an empty 'spoke' turn is a silent degrade -- record status='unavailable' with a machine reason instead
claims.why: Code raises ValueError if status == 'spoke' and content.strip() is empty.
Code raises ValueError if reason is not None for 'spoke'.

claims.text: unavailable needs a machine reason from UNAVAILABLE_REASONS, got {reason!r}
claims.why: Code checks reason not in UNAVAILABLE_REASONS and raises ValueError.

claims.text: A refused turn's stand-in. Carries the rule LABEL only -- never the matched text, never the content, never the evidence paths (the offending path is often the secret).
claims.why: The function sets content to empty string, refs to [], evidence to [], and reason to rule string, so indeed no matched text or evidence paths.

claims.text: anonymous drops even the identity fields, for when the identity itself tripped the floor.
claims.why: When anonymous=True, actor becomes 'council.redacted.redacted', vendor 'redacted', model 'unknown', etc.

claims.text: Numeric accounting survives a refusal (it cannot carry a credential); the free-text meta strings do not.
claims.why: In the non-anonymous case, meta keeps only transport and latency_ms; free-text strings are dropped.

observations.what: _normalize_turn uses _ACTOR_RE which is not defined in this chunk; it may be defined elsewhere in the file.

_normalize_turn references _ALLOWED_TURN_KEYS, TURN_STATUS, MAX_CONTENT_CHARS, UNAVAILABLE_REASONS, ANOMALY_REASONS, ENTRY_VERSION which are not defined in this chunk; they are likely defined elsewhere.
_refusal_receipt references _norm_meta which is defined elsewhere in the file.
